OUR MISSION
Security doesn’t have to lag behind innovation
With Levo, it leads
Words from our founder

“I founded Levo not just to fill a technical gap, but to re-architect how security fits into software development. Growth and security should never be trade-offs. My vision is a world where security is continuous, contextual, and built into the SDLC so innovation never has to slow down. API Security is our first stride towards that vision.”

Buchi Reddy B.
Founder & CEO
Practitioner led team
Built by an engineering leader who refused to choose between growth and security
2016

As Engineering Leader at AppDynamics, Buchi helped unlock $100M+ in quarterly revenue by scaling the platform for enterprise demand.

He led the migration from a monolith to a micro services architecture, making enterprise adoption possible.

To manage this complexity, he led Kubernetes adoption years before it became mainstream.

This exposed him to how APIs, by modularizing functionality and enabling autonomous service scaling, accelerated deployments, integrations, and ultimately revenue growth.

2017

Following the revenue surge driven by platform scalability, AppDynamics was acquired by Cisco.

And what surfaced during Cisco’s security review wasn’t surprising, but it was sobering: missing documentation, untracked APIs, and configuration risks that hadn’t been prioritized.

It was then that Buchi realized how unchecked velocity, while great for business, can damage customer trust and derail business growth.

2020

At Traceable, Buchi began building API specific production tooling but realized that production guardrails were too little too late.

Every vulnerability found post release triggered manual triage, broken SLAs, and customer risk problems that could’ve been avoided with early detection.

What the industry lacked was a scalable and proactive system that could automate all shift left practices so only exploit-proof code reached production.

So he left with one conviction: security must be architected inside the SDLC, not bolted in at the end.

2021

Buchi founded Levo to fix what security had gotten wrong for decades about Software not just for APIs.

He built a security engine that embeds all best practices directly into the SDLC automatically, proactively, continuously, and contextually.

Thereby shattering the assumptions that held AppSec back for decades:
That velocity and security can’t co-exist.
That shift left depends on devs maintaining docs.
That posture improvement requires cloud bloat and manual triage.

Levo was designed not to keep up with Software, but to stay ahead of it.

2023

By 2023, Levo completed the core build of its runtime security platform, laying a strong technical foundation across discovery, visibility, and protection for modern API driven systems. With the platform production ready, Levo initiated its first formal go to market efforts, focusing on real customer environments rather than theoretical use cases.

Early engagement quickly validated strong market pull. Within the first few quarters of launching GTM, Levo.ai closed its first set of customers across North America and India, including large enterprises such as Square and leading fintechs like AngelOne. These early wins confirmed that the market is actively looking for a modern, runtime focused approach to API security that traditional tools were failing to deliver.

2024

In 2024, LEVO moved from early traction to deeper market validation. The first cohort of customers successfully renewed, with product usage and adoption increasing multiple times over as Levo expanded its footprint across production environments. This reinforced confidence not only in the technology, but also in Levo’s ability to deliver sustained value at scale.

During this period, LEVO broadened its customer base to include regulators and large enterprises. The platform was adopted by institutions such as the Insurance Information Bureau of India, along with established organizations including Axis Finance, Axis Bank, and Five9. These deployments further validated LEVO’s relevance across highly regulated industries and complex enterprise environments, marking a clear transition from early adoption to proven enterprise readiness.

2025 AND BEYOND

In 2025, Levo extended its proven runtime security to AI applications.

As enterprises adopted agents, LLMs, MCP servers, and autonomous toolchains, traditional edge controls could not see or explain their behavior.

This created a new risk surface machine-to-machine calls, prompt injection, data leakage, and privilege misuse.

By applying our runtime DNA of kernel level visibility, passive observability, and dynamic security testing, Levo became the first to unify API and AI Security Posture Management.

For enterprises, this meant full coverage and the confidence to scale AI safely, without slowing down the innovation

<script>
/**
 * Global JSON-LD injector for Levo.ai
 * - Adds Organization + WebSite schema on every page
 * - Adds BreadcrumbList on deep paths
 * - Adds Article schema on blog posts (by URL prefix)
 * - Adds Service schema on product/feature/use-case pages (by URL prefixes)
 * - Adds FAQPage schema if FAQ blocks are detected
 * - Normalizes `sameAs` URLs (Twitter/X status -> profile, LinkedIn company root, GitHub org/user root)
 *
 * Place once in: Webflow → Site settings → Custom Code → Head
 * Notes:
 * - This uses client-side JS. It will not appear in "view-source" but will show up in the DOM and in Rich Results Test.
 * - Do not duplicate server-rendered JSON-LD types. The script checks and skips if a type already exists.
 * - You can force the page type with: window.LEVO_PAGE_TYPE = 'article' | 'service' | 'webpage' | 'none'
 */
(function () {
  // -----------------------------
  // CONFIG: edit these as needed
  // -----------------------------
  var SITE = {
    // Public org name in schema
    name: "Levo.ai",

    // Canonical site root (edit if you change domains)
    url: "https://www.levo.ai",

    // Square 512x512 logo used in Organization and as Article publisher logo
    logo512: "https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/68a0867885b861909cb86944/68b99042fdca732433aacf75_logo-512.png",

    // Public profiles for Organization.sameAs (will be normalized below)
    sameAs: [
      "https://www.linkedin.com/company/levo-inc/",
      "https://twitter.com/LevoIncHQ/status/1924518451445420037",
      "https://github.com/levoai"
    ],

    // Blog post base path. If your posts live at /blog/* change this to "/blog"
    blogPrefix: "/post",

    // URL prefixes that should be marked up as Service pages
    // Add/remove to match your IA
    servicePrefixes: [
      "/use-case", "/use-cases", "/usecase", "/usecases",
      "/vertical", "/verticals",
      "/user-story", "/user-stories",
      "/case-study", "/case-studies", "/casestudy",
      "/product", "/products",
      "/feature", "/features",
      "/solutions", "/solution",
      "/platform"
    ]
  };

  // -----------------------------
  // Helper utilities
  // -----------------------------

  // Absolutize a URL relative to current origin
  function abs(u){
    try {
      if (!u) return "";
      return new URL(u, location.origin).href;
    } catch(e){
      return "";
    }
  }

  // Get trimmed textContent for a selector, else empty string
  function text(sel){
    var el = document.querySelector(sel);
    return el ? el.textContent.trim() : "";
  }

  // Get <meta name="..."> content
  function meta(name){
    var el = document.querySelector('meta[name="'+name+'"]');
    return el ? el.content : "";
  }

  // Get <meta property="..."> content (for og:*, article:*, twitter:*)
  function metaProp(p){
    var el = document.querySelector('meta[property="'+p+'"]');
    return el ? el.content : "";
  }

  // Check if a JSON-LD script with a given @type already exists on the page
  // Prevents duplicates when some types are server-rendered by templates
  function hasLDType(t){
    var s = document.querySelectorAll('script[type="application/ld+json"]');
    for (var i=0; i<s.length; i++){
      try {
        var j = JSON.parse(s[i].textContent);
        var arr = Array.isArray(j) ? j : [j];
        for (var k=0; k<arr.length; k++){
          var types = [].concat(arr[k]["@type"] || []);
          if (types.includes(t)) return true;
        }
      } catch(e){
        // Ignore JSON parse errors to avoid blocking the rest
      }
    }
    return false;
  }

  // Append a JSON-LD object to <head>
  function addLD(obj){
    if (!obj) return;
    var s = document.createElement('script');
    s.type = "application/ld+json";
    // No pretty-print to keep payload small
    s.text = JSON.stringify(obj);
    document.head.appendChild(s);
  }

  // Turn "use-case" into "Use Case" for breadcrumbs
  function titleCase(slug){
    return decodeURIComponent(slug)
      .replace(/[-_]+/g, " ")
      .replace(/\b\w/g, function(c){ return c.toUpperCase() });
  }

  // Split path into non-empty segments
  function parts(){
    return location.pathname.split("/").filter(Boolean);
  }

  // True if current path is exactly the prefix or starts with prefix + "/"
  function isPrefix(p){
    return location.pathname === p || location.pathname.startsWith(p + "/");
  }

  // Page classification by path
  function isArticle(){ return isPrefix(SITE.blogPrefix) }
  function isService(){ return SITE.servicePrefixes.some(function(p){ return isPrefix(p) }) }

  /**
   * Normalize Organization.sameAs URLs:
   * - Twitter/X: convert any /status/<id> to profile root /<handle>
   * - LinkedIn company: force /company/<slug>/ with trailing slash
   * - GitHub: collapse /<owner>/<repo> and /orgs/<org> to /<owner|org>
   * - Strip query strings and fragments
   */
  function normalizeSameAs(list){
    return (list || []).map(function(u){
      try {
        var url = new URL(u);
        url.hash = "";
        url.search = "";
        var host = url.hostname.replace(/^www\./,'').toLowerCase();
        var path = url.pathname.replace(/\/+$/,''); // trim trailing slash for logic
        var segs;

        // x.com → twitter.com
        if (host === "x.com") host = "twitter.com";

        // Twitter/X: reduce to profile root /<handle>
        if (host === "twitter.com") {
          segs = path.split("/").filter(Boolean); // /handle[/status/....]
          if (segs.length >= 2 && segs[1] === "status") {
            path = "/" + segs[0];
          } else if (segs.length >= 1) {
            path = "/" + segs[0];
          } else {
            path = "";
          }
        }

        // LinkedIn: force /company/<slug>/
        if (host === "linkedin.com") {
          segs = path.split("/").filter(Boolean);
          var idx = segs.indexOf("company");
          if (idx !== -1 && segs[idx+1]) {
            path = "/company/" + segs[idx+1];
          } else if (segs[0] === "company" && segs[1]) {
            path = "/company/" + segs[1];
          }
          if (/^\/company\/[^\/]+$/.test(path)) path += "/";
        }

        // GitHub: collapse repo/orgs to owner root
        if (host === "github.com") {
          segs = path.split("/").filter(Boolean);
          if (segs[0] === "orgs" && segs[1]) {
            path = "/" + segs[1]; // /orgs/<org> -> /<org>
          } else if (segs.length >= 1) {
            path = "/" + segs[0]; // /<owner>/<repo> -> /<owner>
          } else {
            path = "";
          }
        }

        return "https://" + host + path;
      } catch(e){
        // If URL constructor fails, return original string
        return u;
      }
    });
  }

  // -----------------------------------
  // 1) Organization + WebSite (global)
  // -----------------------------------
  if (!hasLDType("Organization")) {
    addLD({
      "@context":"https://schema.org",
      "@type":"Organization",
      "name": SITE.name,
      "url": SITE.url,
      "logo": {"@type":"ImageObject","url": abs(SITE.logo512)},
      "sameAs": normalizeSameAs(SITE.sameAs)
    });
  }

  if (!hasLDType("WebSite")) {
    addLD({
      "@context":"https://schema.org",
      "@type":"WebSite",
      "name": SITE.name,
      "url": SITE.url,
      // Optional SearchAction. Update target if your site search uses a different route/param.
      "potentialAction": {
        "@type":"SearchAction",
        "target": SITE.url + "/search?query={search_term_string}",
        "query-input":"required name=search_term_string"
      }
    });
  }

  // -------------------------
  // 2) BreadcrumbList (global)
  // -------------------------
  var pp = parts();
  // Add breadcrumbs for any path with at least one segment
  if (pp.length >= 1 && !hasLDType("BreadcrumbList")) {
    var items = [
      {"@type":"ListItem","position":1,"name":"Home","item":SITE.url + "/"}
    ];
    // If it's a blog post, set level 2 as "Blog"
    if (isArticle()){
      items.push({"@type":"ListItem","position":2,"name":"Blog","item": SITE.url + SITE.blogPrefix});
    }
    // Otherwise, if there is at least a folder + page, include the folder as level 2
    else if (pp.length > 1){
      items.push({"@type":"ListItem","position":2,"name": titleCase(pp[0]), "item": SITE.url + "/" + pp[0]});
    }
    // Current page as final crumb
    items.push({
      "@type":"ListItem",
      "position": items.length + 1,
      "name": text("h1") || document.title,
      "item": location.href
    });

    addLD({"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"BreadcrumbList","itemListElement": items});
  }

  // ---------------------------------------------------
  // 3) Decide page type (can be overridden via global)
  // ---------------------------------------------------
  // Manual override example:
  //   window.LEVO_PAGE_TYPE = 'article' | 'service' | 'webpage' | 'none'
  var forced = (window && window.LEVO_PAGE_TYPE) || "";
  var pageType = forced || (isArticle() ? "article" : (isService() ? "service" : "webpage"));

  // -----------------------------------------
  // 4) Article (only for blog posts by prefix)
  // -----------------------------------------
  if (pageType === "article" && !hasLDType("Article")) {
    // Prefer h1 text, fallback to <title>
    var headline = text("h1") || document.title;

    // Use meta description if present
    var description = meta("description") || "";

    // Try a few author sources in order of reliability
    var author = meta("author")
      || text('[rel="author"], .author, .byline, .post-author')
      || SITE.name; // fallback

    // Dates: prefer <time datetime>, fallback to OpenGraph article published/modified
    var datePublished =
      document.querySelector("time[datetime]")?.getAttribute("datetime")
      || metaProp("article:published_time")
      || "";

    var dateModified =
      metaProp("article:modified_time")
      || datePublished
      || "";

    // Image: prefer og:image, then twitter:image
    var image = metaProp("og:image") || meta("twitter:image") || "";

    // Canonical: prefer link[rel=canonical], else current URL
    var canonical = document.querySelector('link[rel="canonical"]')?.href || location.href;

    addLD({
      "@context":"https://schema.org",
      "@type":"Article",
      "headline": headline,
      "description": description || undefined,
      "author": [{"@type":"Person","name": author}],
      "publisher": {
        "@type":"Organization",
        "name": SITE.name,
        "logo": {"@type":"ImageObject","url": abs(SITE.logo512)}
      },
      "datePublished": datePublished || undefined,
      "dateModified": dateModified || undefined,
      "image": image ? [abs(image)] : undefined,
      "mainEntityOfPage": {"@type":"WebPage","@id": canonical},
      "url": canonical
    });
  }

  // -------------------------------------------------------------------
  // 5) Service (use-case, vertical, user-story, product, feature, etc.)
  // -------------------------------------------------------------------
  if (pageType === "service" && !hasLDType("Service")) {
    var sHeadline = text("h1") || document.title;

velocity, while great for business, can damage customer trust and derail business growth.</strong></p></div></div></div><div role="listitem" class="timeline_list-item w-dyn-item"><div realized that production guardrails were too little too late.</p><p>Every vulnerability found post release triggered manual triage, broken SLAs, and customer risk problems that could’ve been avoided with early detection.</p><p>What the industry lacked was a scalable and proactive system that could automate all shift left practices so only exploit-proof code reached production.</p><p>So he left with one conviction: <strong>security must be architected inside the SDLC, not bolted in at the end.</strong></p></div></div></div><div role="listitem" class="timeline_list-item w-dyn-item"><div Software not just for APIs.</p><p>He built a <strong>security engine</strong> that embeds all best practices directly into the SDLC automatically, proactively, continuously, and contextually.</p><p>Thereby shattering the assumptions that held AppSec back for decades:<br>That velocity and security can’t co-exist.<br>That shift left depends on devs maintaining docs.<br>That posture improvement requires cloud bloat and manual triage.</p><p><strong>Levo was designed not to keep up with Software, but to stay ahead of it.</strong></p></div></div></div><div role="listitem" class="timeline_list-item w-dyn-item"><div class="subtitle-gradient">2023</div><div class="timeline_card"><div class="timeline_rich-text w-richtext"><p>By 2023, Levo completed the core build of its This reinforced confidence not only in the technology, but also in Levo’s ability to deliver sustained value at scale.</p><p>During this period, LEVO <strong>broadened its customer base to include regulators and large enterprises</strong>. enterprise readiness.</p></div></div></div><div role="listitem" class="timeline_list-item w-dyn-item"><div class="subtitle-gradient">2025 and Beyond</div><div class="timeline_card"><div
